question: True or false: an OLED's seal must stop water vapour about a million times better than food-packaging film?
answer: True. Traces of water ruin OLED materials and their reactive electrodes, so the target is about a millionth of a gram per square metre per day, while food films pass between a tenth of a gram and several grams. Thin-film seals stack ceramic and polymer layers so the next caps any pinhole.
move: Size a barrier by how little of the threat does damage.
trap: Judging from familiar packaging, a few times tighter seems plenty.

diagram.unit: µg water per m² a day
diagram.caption: Food films pass a tenth of a gram to several grams; the OLED seal a millionth.

reference: Lewis & Weaver, Thin-film permeation-barrier technology for flexible organic light-emitting devices, IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics 10(1), 2004
